title: Strip three patches of old paint off a window sash: one hand keeps the heat gun on the paint while the other scrapes it
instruction: Strip the three patches of old paint off the window sash's near rail with the heat gun and the scraper: with one hand hold the heat gun aimed at a patch, a few centimetres from it, until the paint blisters, and keep it there while the other hand pushes the scraper's blade along the rail through the patch to take the soft paint off; then do the next patch, and the last. Never point the heat gun at the glass. Then stand the heat gun back on its stand, lay the scraper back with its handle on its rest, and take both arms back to where they started.
context: Decorators and joiners restoring old windows strip paint with a heat gun and a scraper. Old paint softens only while it is hot and hardens again within seconds, so one hand keeps the heat on the paint while the other scrapes it; aimed at the glass, the heat cracks the pane.
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them. (1) A grey cotton dust sheet 2 mm thick covering the table from 11 to 51 cm forward and from 32 cm right to 32 cm left. (2) A pine window sash, 28 cm front to back, 34 cm across and 3 cm thick, with rails 4.5 cm wide, lying flat on the dust sheet from 18.5 to 46.5 cm forward and from 17 cm right to 17 cm left, its top 3.2 cm above the table, fixed. It has been stripped to bare wood. Its 4 mm float glass pane (19 by 25 cm, light green-blue) sits in the rebate with putty round it, its top 1 cm below the sash's top. (3) Three patches of old cream gloss paint, cracked and flaking, 6 cm long and 3.4 cm across, on the sash's near rail (its middle line 20.75 cm forward), centred 7.5 cm left, on the centre line and 7.5 cm right. (4) An orange 2000 W heat gun (0.40 kg, 20 cm long: a plastic housing 13 cm long, 4.8 cm wide and 5.6 cm tall, a steel nozzle 3.1 cm across, a black pistol grip raked back below it), already running, lying on a black steel stand at 25 cm forward and 25 cm left, its nozzle pointing toward the near right (40 degrees round from straight back toward the right), its housing's axis 9.5 cm above the table. (5) A paint scraper (0.20 kg): a beech handle 13.4 cm long, 2 cm wide and 2.2 cm deep with a red end cap, and a steel head holding a 4 cm wide carbide-edged blade that slopes forward and down to its edge; it lies along the table 30 cm forward, its blade's edge on the sheet 21.2 cm right of the centre line and its handle toward the right, its end cap on a beech rest block 2 cm tall. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Heat: the gun heats what its nozzle points at, within 10 cm of the nozzle's tip: a patch when its axis meets the rail within 2 cm of the patch. A patch's heat rises by 0.5 per second while it is heated and falls by 0.5 per second otherwise (between 0 and 1.6); it is blistered from 1.0 (2 s of heat) until its heat falls below 0.6. Pointed at the glass within 10 cm for a total of 1 s, the glass cracks. Scraping: the paint comes off where the blade's edge passes through a blistered patch while the edge is on the wood (from 4 mm below to 7 mm above the rail's top), over the rail's middle (within 1.2 cm) and within 15 degrees of level across; a patch is stripped once the blade has passed over 80 percent of its length (24 of its 30 2 mm strips). The heat gun is back on its stand when it lies within 4 cm of where it started, tilted no more than 10 degrees; the scraper is back when it lies within 3 cm of where it started, tilted no more than 8 degrees. 0.0 once the glass has cracked. Otherwise, at the end: 1.0 with all three patches stripped, the heat gun back on its stand, the scraper back on its rest and both arms back where they started (each gripper's fingertip centre within 5 cm of its start); 0.5 with all three patches stripped; 0.25 with at least one stripped; else 0.0. A stripped patch stays stripped. The trial ends at the run limit, or once the full score has held for 1 s with the heat gun and the scraper still.
reset_notes: Paint three fresh patches of old cream paint on the near rail, check the glass is whole, stand the heat gun back on its stand and lay the scraper back with its handle on its rest.
fidelity: Rigid-body simulation (Isaac Sim 6.1, PhysX, 20 Hz control). Simplified: heat and paint are modelled by rule: each patch keeps a heat value from where the gun's nozzle points, and its paint is taken off where the scraper's edge passes while it is blistered (the patches, blisters and lifted flakes are drawn). The gun's centre of mass is under the hand on its housing. The sash, stand and rest are fixed. Cameras 1280 x 704 (Dream-1 sees 320 x 176).
